issues.description: trainer_args key mismatch: docstring promises max_steps/val_interval, code reads max_step and never references val_interval
issues.detail: The DeepSpeedTrainer.__init__ docstring lists trainer_args keys as max_steps, log_interval, val_interval, save_interval, but the implementation reads trainer_args['max_step'] (singular) and never reads val_interval at all. log_interval is also read but not used. Validation cadence is silently bound to save_interval. A caller following the documented contract will KeyError on max_step, and the documented val_interval semantics are absent. Pick one schema, make code and docstring agree, and remove unused keys.

issues.description: run() loop has no termination/progress guarantee and can overshoot max_step or spin forever
issues.detail: The outer `while self.global_step < self.max_step` loop relies on train() advancing global_step by save_interval, with no per-step max_step check inside train() and no progress assertion. If train()'s iterator yields zero batches (empty shard, exhausted state), global_step never increments and the loop spins forever writing identical checkpoints. If save_interval does not divide max_step, training overshoots by up to save_interval-1 steps. State and enforce the invariant that each outer iteration strictly advances global_step, and bound the inner length by min(save_interval, max_step - global_step).

issues.description: _all_reduce_stats mutates caller's dict/tensors in place with unstated and unenforced cross-rank preconditions
issues.detail: The function iterates `for key in stats` issuing async all_reduces, then divides in place by world_size. Collective communication requires every rank to call the same collectives in the same order with the same shapes/dtypes/devices, but nothing enforces identical key sets/order across ranks (a single optional metric on one rank deadlocks the job). The function also silently mutates the caller's `out['stats']` object, conflating value with identity, and asserts type but not device/dtype/shape. Return a new dict (or document the frame explicitly), pack stats into a single fixed-shape tensor and reduce once, and validate consistency.

issues.description: Validation averaging is unweighted across batches (mean-of-batch-means rather than sample-weighted mean)
issues.detail: valid() appends per-batch scalar stats into lists and reports sum(values)/len(values). For variable-size batches (typical with length-bucketed batchfy/collate_fn padding), this is a batch-weighted average that silently disagrees with the true validation mean. The author's own inline comment hints they know there's a bug. Track (sum, count) pairs and divide once, or weight by batch size / token count. Also guard against empty datasets (ZeroDivisionError) and NaN poisoning.

issues.description: Checkpoint discovery uses fragile substring + int() parsing of directory names
issues.detail: _load_checkpoint filters with `'step_' in d.name` (substring) and sorts by `int(x.name.split('step_')[-1])`. Names like `pre_step_warmup`, `step_100_backup`, or `step_final` either get included incorrectly or crash with ValueError mid-startup. Use a strict regex/prefix match (`startswith('step_')` plus a try/except on the int parse), or write a manifest file / `latest` symlink to make 'latest checkpoint' explicit rather than place-encoded.

issues.description: wandb is documented as MANDATORY but the precondition is never enforced, coupling trainer to global state
issues.detail: The class docstring states the trainer 'will raise an error if wandb.run is None', but no such check exists; wandb.config.update and wandb.log are called unconditionally and will fail with opaque attribute errors if the precondition is violated. Beyond enforcement, hard-wiring wandb-as-global telemetry into the trainer conflates 'metric produced' with 'metric shipped to wandb'. Either add the assert the docstring promises, or pass a logger callback/sink list so the trainer can be tested and reused without wandb.

issues.description: freeze_param uses string-prefix matching on parameter names with no zero-match warning
issues.detail: Matching is `k.startswith(t + '.') or k == t`, a leaky abstraction over PyTorch's dotted-name convention. A typo in a freeze pattern silently freezes nothing and training proceeds, producing the classic 'why is my fine-tune not converging' bug. Resolve patterns against `model.get_submodule()` / `named_modules()`, and log or assert per-pattern match counts >0.

issues.description: Specifier parsing uses undocumented whitespace split() and is applied inconsistently between train and valid paths
issues.detail: `args.valid_unregistered_specifier.split()` splits on whitespace, but the help text documents specs as `task:name:data_json[:factor]` with no mention that multiple specs are space-separated. Paths containing spaces are silently misparsed. The train path passes a single string; valid splits into many — the CLI surface is inconsistent. Document the separator explicitly, switch to `nargs='+'` or a structured (YAML/JSON) list of {task, name, json, factor} entries, and apply uniformly.

issues.description: torch.cuda.set_device(args.local_rank) runs before validating that local_rank was set
issues.detail: args.local_rank defaults to None and the help text admits the launcher is supposed to set it. If the launcher uses LOCAL_RANK env var instead of the flag, or the user runs the script directly, `torch.cuda.set_device(None)` raises an opaque TypeError before any logging is configured. Fall back to the LOCAL_RANK env var and assert local_rank is a non-negative int < device_count with a clear error message.

issues.description: _load_checkpoint silently falls back to latest on disk when an explicit resume_path does not exist
issues.detail: The logic is: if resume_path and resume_path.exists() -> use it; elif checkpoints dir exists -> use latest. A typo or wrong mount in `--resume_path` silently resumes a different run rather than failing loudly. Optional[Path] cannot distinguish 'no request' from 'request that failed'. Raise on a missing explicit resume_path, or at minimum log loudly that fallback is occurring.

issues.description: train_dtype casts inputs under amp, conflating engine training dtype with input cast dtype
issues.detail: When amp is enabled, the function returns bf16/fp16 and to_device casts inputs to that dtype. PyTorch and DeepSpeed AMP expect fp32 inputs and manage per-op precision via autocast; pre-casting at minimum bypasses amp's intended semantics and at worst causes dtype-mismatch errors inside the model. Only cast under explicit fp16/bf16 modes, or document why amp intentionally casts inputs. Also consider deriving dtype from the initialized engine (single source of truth) rather than re-parsing ds_config.

issues.description: Mixed kebab-case and snake_case CLI flags (--train-config vs --local_rank/--resume_path)
issues.detail: Most flags use kebab-case (--train-config, --output-dir) but --local_rank and --resume_path use snake_case. Argparse normalizes both to underscore attributes so it works, but the user-facing surface is inconsistent. Pick one convention; --local_rank is launcher-imposed, so either match snake elsewhere or document it as an exception.

issues.description: train_dtype is an instance method but does not use self
issues.detail: train_dtype is a pure function of ds_config with no use of self. Promote to a module-level helper or @staticmethod (or a small config ADT with a .dtype property) so the dependency is explicit and it can be tested independently of the trainer.

issues.description: No tests in the diff for pure-Python helpers that are testable
issues.detail: _load_checkpoint's sorting logic, _all_reduce_stats' tensor handling shape, train_dtype's branching, and the specifier parser are all amenable to unit tests despite the distributed setting. Add a handful of pure-Python tests.

issues.description: Non-rank-0 log level set to CRITICAL loses crash context from other ranks
issues.detail: Setting log_level='CRITICAL' on all non-zero ranks means when one rank crashes, you get nothing from it. Keep WARNING at minimum, or write per-rank log files. Silence-by-default on stdout is fine; losing crash context is not.

issues.description: valid_iterator_args is a shared dict reused across factory constructions via **kwargs
issues.detail: valid_iterator_args is reused across two loops with **valid_iterator_args. If a future DataIteratorFactory mutates kwargs or a held object (collate_fn), bugs become invisible. Promote to a typed struct (NamedTuple/dataclass) or pass explicit named kwargs at the call site to make the contract explicit.

issues.description: main() lacks try/finally around distributed init and wandb cleanup
issues.detail: deepspeed.init_distributed, model/dataloader construction, and trainer.run() can all raise. wandb.finish() is only reached on the happy path, leaking offline runs. More importantly, no try/finally surrounds torch.distributed cleanup — a rank crashing mid-training leaves siblings hanging at the next collective. Wrap startup and run in try/finally with explicit teardown.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges on NEEDS-WORK before merge. Two P0 issues are unanimous: the trainer_args schema is inconsistent (docstring says max_steps/val_interval but code reads max_step and never references val_interval, with validation silently bound to save_interval), and run()'s termination/progress invariants are unstated and unenforced (can overshoot max_step or spin forever on an empty iterator). _all_reduce_stats mutates caller state in place with unstated and unenforced cross-rank preconditions that will deadlock NCCL on the first divergence. P1 cluster: validation averaging is batch-weighted rather than sample-weighted; checkpoint discovery via substring+int parsing is fragile; wandb is mandatory in prose but never asserted and tightly coupled to the trainer; freeze_param prefix-matching silently no-ops on typos; specifier parsing uses undocumented whitespace splits applied inconsistently between train and valid; local_rank=None reaches torch.cuda.set_device with no early check; explicit resume_path silently falls back to disk; train_dtype conflates engine dtype with input casting under amp. Fixes are mostly stating and enforcing contracts rather than redesign.
